findings.title: The design copies one particular book series' structure, not just the genre: race and class picked on floor 3, loot boxes that only open in safe rooms, six box tiers, fan boxes at follower milestones, a three-step boss ladder by area, and a talk show between floors
findings.where: docs/DESIGN.md:111 (Role and makeover, floor 3), :169 (crates sealed until a green room), :37 (tiers Copper…Starlight), :188-190 and section 7 (district / zone / floor boss); in the game: magic.tab.role.none, magic.casting.too_early, npc.hint.crate.text, show.line.fans_milestone.*, show.interview.*
findings.what_happens: Dungeon Crawler Carl is the work whose names fill most of NAMES_NOT_ALLOWED.txt (Carl, Donut, Mordecai, Odette…). A reader who knows it will see that work here: crawlers choose a 'role' (class) and a 'makeover' (race) on the third floor, as Carl does on floor 3. Prize crates are won on the spot but stay sealed until a green room, like loot boxes that only open in a saferoom. There are six crate tiers ending above Diamond in 'Starlight', against Bronze…Legendary/Celestial. Fan Mail crates come at fan milestones, like fan boxes. District, zone and floor bosses mirror neighbourhood, borough and floor bosses. Between floors a talk-show host interviews the crawler on a couch, like Odette's show. DESIGN §2 allows the genre (deadly crawl as a game show with host, loot boxes, achievements, audience, sponsors) but not one work's concrete rules.
findings.evidence: I read DESIGN.md §1–8 against the texts that put these rules on screen. Example: magic.tab.role.none says 'The Casting Office opens on floor %s: the Casting Desk for a role, the Makeover Chair for a new look', and DESIGN §7 fixes it at depth 3. I am not sure the owner counts these as genre. Each one alone is small; together they are that work's skeleton. Own alternatives that cost little: open the Casting Office on the first floor that has a boss down, or at a fixed Hype mark, instead of depth 3; let crates open anywhere off combat after a countdown ('the crew needs ten seconds to cut the tape'); name the boss ranks by show terms ('Guest Star / Special Guest / Headliner'); make the couch an occasional reward rather than a between-floor fixture. This is a decision for the lead.

I read all 16 lang files on lane-a after rebasing on origin/claude/determined-edison-xwiksi, key by key. I also read the 1,000 lines of the spoken script: every line whose text differs from its lang key, plus the identical ones through their keys. I checked about twenty specific claims against the code or data. These match: 3 points a level (Rules.POINTS_PER_LEVEL), stairs locked for the first quarter of airtime (RunConfig.stairsLockedShare 0.25), 10 floors (RunConfig.floors and Places.DEPTHS), casting from floor 3, sponsors from floor 4, sidekicks from floor 2, the Floor Plan's 7x7 tiles, the buckler (0.05 s, 70°) and riot shield (0.25 s, 100°, +2 armour), every weapon's damage, speed and reach in GearItems, the per-point stat numbers and +1.5% per skill level in Rules, crits at 150%, wager altars in green rooms (HighRoller.java), and the bell_ringer and vault technique data. These do not match: what skills do, bombs hurting their thrower, where points can be spent, and what sponsor challenges count (findings below). /home/user/shots/TEXTS/ does not exist, so I looked at the TUTORIAL pictures at full size (o05, o16, o17). I made no change to the repository, ran no game test and no client run: each claim rests on code reading, the scans and the existing pictures. This lens has no limit of eight findings, so the findings below are grouped by kind.

findings.title: The Skills tab and skill-up toasts promise effects the game does not have: 6 of 24 skills do nothing, and all 96 'unlock' texts at levels 5/10/15/20 unlock nothing
findings.where: profile/assets/crawloffame/lang/en_us.json: profile.skill.alchemy.desc, .tinkering.desc, .pathfinding.desc, .showmanship.desc, .sneaking.desc, .dodging.desc, and every profile.skill.<id>.tier.5/.10/.15/.20 (24 x 4 = 96 keys). Shown by src/client/java/net/kasax/crawl/client/profile/ClientProfile.java:31-33 (toast) and SkillsTab.java:97-99 (tooltip, green when reached)
findings.what_happens: At skill level 10 a toast says, for example, 'Tycoon: vendors pay you to shop', 'Companion: your pets follow you down the stairs', 'Winter star: it snows when you enter', 'Safety third: your own blasts hurt you less' or 'Extras: one more summon at a time'. The Skills tab marks these lines green as unlocked. None of it happens. Alchemy is described as 'Brewing potions at the Alchemy Stand' and Tinkering as 'Building bombs and gadgets at the Tinker's Bench'; neither station exists (docs/PLAN.md:50 lists them as unbuilt). Pathfinding, Showmanship ('+1.5% more Hype per level'), Sneaking ('+1.5% less noticed') and Dodging ('+1.5% chance per level to avoid a hit') give no bonus at all.
findings.evidence: Rules.THRESHOLDS {5,10,15,20} is used only by Rules.thresholdAt and the two client classes above; no server code reads a threshold (grep THRESHOLDS/thresholdAt in src/main/java). Skill bonuses are applied only for ATHLETICS and BLOCKING (ProfileModule.java:88-93), ARCHERY and melee skills (Combat.java:57-59), EXPLOSIVES (Blast.java:41), THROWING (ThrownKnife.java:53), FIRST_AID (BandageItem.java:34), BARTERING (Shops.java:138), BEAST_HANDLING (Sidekicks.java:88), TRAP_HANDLING (Traps.java:549) and the magic schools (Casting.java:62). Grepping src/main/java and src/client/java for Skill.ALCHEMY, TINKERING, PATHFINDING and SHOWMANSHIP finds nothing; SNEAKING and DODGING are only trained, never read (Secrets.java:110, Traps.java:152, Shrines.java:245). No Java file mentions an alchemy stand or a tinker's bench. docs/DESIGN.md:107 says only that 'Each level gives a small bonus to what the skill does'. Fix: rewrite the tier lines as titles with no promised effect (for example 'Tycoon' alone), and say in the six descs that the skill does nothing yet, or hide those six skills until it does. None of these texts is recorded.

They cover: lighting a pyro crate and tipping a drum by use and by hit as an adventure-mode crawler; arrows shot at a hanging load, a cleat and a pyro crate; a cast member who joins after the key carrier died; six cuts of the Rehearsal Wing rig; and props counted on generated plans of the Understage, Hollowmere Manor and the Sun Tomb at depths 1, 5 and 9 (up to 14 combat rooms each), with 300 rolls of each prop table and of each room's monster group. I found no repeat-loot path: relogs, restarts, two crawlers searching the same prop, a full bag and a run's end were all sound. Searching through a wall needs a modified client, because the server checks reach but not line of sight. I could not show bosses being trivialised, because pieces go only in COMBAT rooms. The pictures are /home/user/shots/ROOMS1/strips; every piece in them was set off by `/crawl setpiece fire`, not by a player's hand.

findings.title: A pyro crate cannot be lit by hand: the hint says "[use] Light the fuse", but neither use nor a hit does anything. Only a crawler's projectile lights one.
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/setpiece/PieceBlocks.java:249-274 (Pyro has no useWithoutItem); SetpieceModule.java:191-202 (AttackBlockCallback); world/Protection.java:25; client/setpiece/SearchHud.java:145-160
findings.what_happens: A melee or caster crawler looks at a red crate, sees "[use] Light the fuse · or shoot it", presses use and nothing happens. Hitting it does nothing either. Crates (and the manor's lamp-oil casks and the tomb's oil jars) work only for a crawler with a bow or thrown weapon. Oil drums advertise "or hit it", but hitting one does nothing too.
findings.evidence: Scratch test rv_setpiece_game_tests_pyro_by_hand used a real crawler in a run (game mode adventure), through ServerPlayerGameMode.useItemOn and handleBlockBreakAction. Log: "client restricted true, attack callback Fail[]; pyro after use lit=false; drum after use tipped=true; pyro after hit lit=false; drum after hit tipped=false". The code agrees: Pyro does not override useWithoutItem. The world module's Protection registers its AttackBlockCallback first and returns FAIL for any block outside crawloffame:breakable, so setpiece's attack listener never runs for a crawler. In adventure mode the client also refuses to send the attack, because Player.blockActionRestricted is true. Every engineer test calls Pieces.light() directly, and the crawltest uses `/crawl setpiece fire blast`.

findings.title: Searching a room pays two to three times what its monsters drop, not "about a third more" as the report and BALANCE 7 claim.
findings.where: docs/BALANCE.md:236-241 and tools/content/setpiece/loot.py:6 (the budget) against src/main/modules/item/data/crawloffame/crawl/loot/monster/{minion,regular,elite}.json and src/main/modules/setpiece/data/crawloffame/crawl/loot/setpiece/*.json
findings.what_happens: A crawler who searches every prop roughly doubles to triples their items, and in studio and manor places their coins, compared with one who only fights. In a cast every member gets the full prop loot, while monster drops fall once for the whole cast, so the gap grows with each friend.
findings.evidence: Scratch test rv_economy_game_tests_economy generated real plans and counted the placed props, then rolled 300 times per prop and per Director.group. Per combat room, items from props versus monsters: Understage d1 2.89 vs 1.14 (+253 %), d5 3.01 vs 1.36 (+221 %), d9 2.90 vs 1.90 (+153 %). Manor d1/d5/d9: +201 %, +162 %, +125 %. Sun Tomb d1/d5/d9: +202 %, +161 %, +115 %. Coins from props versus monsters: Understage d5 12.6 vs 4.8 (+264 %), d9 18.2 vs 9.6 (+189 %); Manor d5 16.7 vs 5.2 (+320 %), d9 31.7 vs 12.6 (+251 %); Tomb d5 +46 %, d9 +55 %. The doc's premise that a monster drops "about 1.5 items" is wrong: the tables give 0.15 (minion), 0.3 (regular) and 1.5 only for an elite. Meanwhile a tool chest, a lost-and-found bin or a craft trolley averages 1.35 to 1.5 stacks, not "a third of an item". The rolls do follow depth bands, not the place.

findings.title: A cast member who reaches the floor after the key carrier died never gets that safe's key.
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/setpiece/Keys.java:125-138 (died) and 48-89 (each room is keyed once)
findings.what_happens: Crawlers go down the stairs one at a time (DESIGN: "Each crawler goes down alone"), and friends may join on floor 1 for five minutes. Whoever arrives after the carrier's death gets "Locked. One of the monsters in this room carries the key." for the rest of the floor. No monster ever carries that key again, so their only option is the lockpick. This is the opposite of the report's "its death keys every living member" and the Emcee line "copies cut for the whole cast".
findings.evidence: Keys.died hands keys only to members who are alive and on mo.floor() at the moment of death, and the room goes into FloorState "keyed" so no second carrier is chosen. Scratch test rv_setpiece_game_tests_late_member_gets_no_key: crawler A, carrier killed, then B joins through the same Stage Door. Log: "same cast true, a has key true, b has key false, b opened the safe false".

findings.title: Rigs cannot be shot, although the hint says "Cut the rope · or shoot it". The hanging load and the cleat have no collision box, so arrows fly straight through.
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/setpiece/PieceBlocks.java:64-68 (LOAD_BLOCK noCollision), 131-135 (Cleat collision empty), 149-151 and 176-179 (onProjectileHit that never fires); SearchHud.java:141-144
findings.what_happens: An archer aims at a stage lamp, a sandbag, a manor chandelier or a tomb stone, or at its cleat, as the HUD invites. The arrow passes through and nothing drops. The only way left is to walk to the wall and press use on the cleat, so the brief's "shoot the rope" from range is impossible.
findings.evidence: Scratch test rv_setpiece_game_tests_shoot_the_rig fired a crawler-owned Arrow at a load, at a cleat and at a pyro crate. Log: "shot at load: cleat cut false, load still hanging_load; shot at cleat: cut false; shot at pyro: scorch_mark". Vanilla projectiles hit blocks only through ClipContext.Block.COLLIDER (ProjectileUtil.java:35/60), and the mod's SpellBolt.java:112 uses COLLIDER too, so an empty collision shape is never hit.

findings.title: The Rehearsal Wing's rig re-hangs every five seconds, and each cut trains Stagecraft, so the skill can be farmed without end in a room with no clock and no danger.
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/orientation/WingRig.java:25-41 with setpiece/Pieces.java:115-120 (used(): Profiles.train STAGECRAFT +2 on every cut)
findings.what_happens: A crawler stands in the dress set and uses the cleat every five seconds. Stagecraft XP rises with every cut, and the skill keeps the +3 % per level piece damage for the whole career. The wing stops the airtime and nobody can die there, so it costs nothing. No other wing beat trains a skill.
findings.evidence: Scratch test rv_setpiece_game_tests_wing_rig_trains_for_ever used a crawler tagged to rehearse, in the wing, with the real use path on the wing's cleat every 180 ticks. Log: "cuts 6 ... xp 2 ... xp 4 ... xp 6 ... xp 8 ... xp 10 ... xp 12", and the rope was uncut again before every use.

findings.title: The prop crate's debris kind exists but is never placed. Breaking a crate still gives one roll to whoever broke it, with no debris and nothing for the rest of the cast.
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/setpiece/Kind.java:25 and 68 (CRATE_DEBRIS); item/block/PropCrateBlock.java:42-55 (unchanged since 7424c4d); report ROOMS1.md:9-12, docs/DESIGN.md:230, DATAPACKS.md:105
findings.what_happens: The brief asks for the prop crate to be "breakable by weapon, with debris", and the report counts "prop-crate debris" among its 21 kinds. In the game a smashed crate just vanishes and pops a single container/prop_crate roll at the smasher's feet, so friends still race each other for crates. In fact there are 20 kinds, 11 of them studio kinds.
findings.evidence: A grep for CRATE_DEBRIS and crate_debris in src/main/java finds only Kind, SearchBlock and Searches (sounds). No painter, block or event ever sets the block. PropCrateBlock.smash/drop is untouched by any ROOMS1 commit (git log on the file shows only 7424c4d).

findings.title: A monster the room set on fire that dies of the burn is not a set kill: no Hype, no Emcee, no crowd, no Stagecraft
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/setpiece/Pieces.java:178 (credit only if the killing source is SET_PIECE with the crawler as its entity); fire set at :327 (blast, 2 s) and :392 (burning slick, 3 s)
findings.what_happens: A good oil-and-pyro combo: a crawler lights the slick, and a weakened monster walks out burning and dies a second later. It dies to vanilla on-fire damage, which has no attacker. Pieces.died returns at once, so the show ignores the best use of the room. The kill does not count for 'One Big Bang' either (set.multi counts only deaths inside the blast tick).
findings.evidence: Code path: inSlick() hits for BURN_BASE every 10 ticks only while the monster stands in the slick, then igniteForSeconds(3). explode() ignites survivors for 2 s. AFTER_DEATH → Pieces.died(e, source), where source is level.damageSources().onFire() with getEntity()==null, so it returns before Stats/Hype/Crowd/Emcee. LAST.remove has already cleared the piece.
